## Answers

### isbn-checksum

The ISBN checksum is validated in the `isValid` method of the `IsbnValidator` class [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/IsbnValidator.java:13-31

### isbn-prefix

According to the `IsbnValidator` class, only ISBN-13 numbers with the prefixes "978" or "979" are accepted for books [3].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/IsbnValidator.java:13-31

### isbn-hyphens

Yes, users can enter ISBNs with hyphens or spaces. This is handled by the `normalize` method in `IsbnValidator.java` [1], which removes any hyphens or spaces before validating the ISBN.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/IsbnValidator.java:3-33

### add-book

When a book with an existing ISBN is added again, the `addBook` method in `BookService` [1] checks if the book already exists in the repository [3] by calling `findByIsbn(normalized)`. If the book exists, it adds the specified number of copies to the existing book and saves the updated book [1]. If the book does not exist, it creates a new book with the provided details and saves it [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/BookService.java:17-33, src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/BookRepository.java:6-19

### future-year

Yes, books with a publication year in the future are rejected. This is checked in the `addBook` method of `BookService.java` [1], where it throws an `InvalidBookException` if the publication year is after the current year.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/BookService.java:17-33

### copies-available

The system checks if a copy of a book is available by calling the `isAvailable()` method on the `Book` object. This method returns `true` if `availableCopies` is greater than 0, indicating that there are copies available for checkout [7].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/Book.java:30-32

### return-copy-guard

The method `returnCopy()` in `Book.java` prevents returning more copies than the library owns by checking if `availableCopies` is equal to `totalCopies`. If they are equal, it throws an `IllegalStateException` indicating that all copies are already on the shelf [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/Book.java:42-47

### find-by-author

`findByAuthor` returns a list of `Book` objects that match the given author. The author is matched case-insensitively [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/book/BookRepository.java:6-19

### loan-limit

When a member tries to borrow more books than allowed, the `LoanService#checkout(UUID, String)` method throws a `LoanLimitExceededException` [1]. This exception is thrown if the number of active loans for the member exceeds the maximum allowed by their membership tier.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/LoanService.java:50-75

### tier-limits

A premium member can borrow up to 10 books at once. This is determined by the `maxActiveLoans` value for the `PREMIUM` tier in the `MembershipTier` enum [3].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MembershipTier.java:3-26

### grace-period

Yes, premium members get a grace period on late returns. This is specified in the `MembershipTier` enum where the `PREMIUM` tier has a grace period of 2 days [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MembershipTier.java:3-26

### fine-calculation

Late fees are calculated in the `FineCalculator` class. The `calculate` method computes the number of days a book is overdue by subtracting the grace days of the member's tier from the difference between the due date and the return date. If the book is returned on time or within the grace period, no fine is charged. Otherwise, a fine is calculated by multiplying the number of late days by the fine per day set in the `LibraryProperties`. The fine is then capped at the maximum fine per loan to prevent excessively high fines for lost or found books. [1][3]

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/FineCalculator.java:25-32, src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/LibraryProperties.java:9-25

### fine-cap

Yes, there is a maximum fine for a single overdue loan. This is defined in the `LibraryProperties` class [1], where the `maxFinePerLoan` parameter is set to a default value of `10.00`.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/LibraryProperties.java:9-25

### fine-rounding

Fine amounts are rounded to two decimal places using `RoundingMode.HALF_UP` [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/FineCalculator.java:25-32

### loan-period

The default loan period is 14 days, as specified in the `LibraryProperties` class [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/LibraryProperties.java:9-25

### suspension

A member gets suspended when the total amount of unpaid fines reaches or exceeds the configured suspension threshold. This is checked in the `chargeFine` method in `MemberService.java` [5].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MemberService.java:37-47

### reinstate

A suspended member gets their borrowing rights back by paying off their outstanding fines. This is handled in the `payFines` method of the `MemberService` class [5]. When a member pays fines, the `payFines` method checks if the member's outstanding fines are below the suspension threshold. If they are, the member's suspension is lifted using the `reinstate` method, and the member is saved back to the repository.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MemberService.java:49-56

### suspended-checkout

No, a suspended member cannot check out a book. This is enforced in the `LoanService#checkout` method, where the first check is if the member is suspended:

```java
if (member.isSuspended()) {
    throw new MemberSuspendedException();
}
```

If a member is suspended, a `MemberSuspendedException` is thrown, preventing the checkout process.

Citations: none

### suspended-status

The HTTP status returned when a suspended member tries to borrow is `FORBIDDEN` [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/web/ApiErrorHandler.java:37-42

### duplicate-loan

No, a member cannot borrow two copies of the same title. This is enforced by the `LoanService#checkout` method, which checks if the member already holds the book with `loans.existsActiveByMemberAndIsbn(memberId, book.isbn())`. If this condition is true, it throws an `AlreadyBorrowedException`.

Citations: none

### checkout-order

The borrowing rules are checked in the following order during the checkout process:

1. The member is not suspended.
2. The member is under their tier's active-loan limit.
3. The member does not already hold this title.
4. A copy of the book is available.

These checks are performed in the `checkout` method of the `LoanService` class, as shown in the code snippet from `LoanService.java` [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/LoanService.java:50-75

### due-date

The due date of a new loan is computed by adding the loan period to the date the book is borrowed. This is done in the `Loan` constructor, where the `dueOn` field is set to the current date plus the loan period [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/Loan.java:24-30

### return-flow

When a book is returned late, the `returnBook` method in the `LoanService` class is called. This method calculates a late fine based on the loan period and the current date. If the fine is greater than zero, it charges the fine to the member's account using the `memberService.chargeFine` method. The fine amount is returned by the `returnBook` method.

Citations: none

### double-return

If the same loan is returned twice, the system will throw an `IllegalStateException` with the message "Loan [loanId] was already returned". This is because the `returnBook` method checks if the loan is active before marking it as returned. If the loan is already marked as returned, it will throw this exception to prevent duplicate returns.

Citations: none

### renew-rules

Renewing a loan is not allowed if the loan is overdue or if the maximum number of renewals has been reached. This is checked in the `LoanService#renew(UUID)` method [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/LoanService.java:97-110

### max-renewals

A loan can be renewed up to the number of times specified by the `maxRenewals` property in the `LibraryProperties` class. This value is set by default to 2 [3].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/LibraryProperties.java:9-25

### reminder-schedule

Due date reminder emails are sent every morning at 08:00 [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/DueDateReminderJob.java:14-58

### reminder-duplicates

The reminder job avoids emailing the same reminder twice after a crash by marking the reminder as sent before sending it. This is done in the `sendReminders` method, where the line `loan.markReminderSent();` is executed before sending the notification. If the job crashes mid-run, the loan will still be marked as sent, and the next time the job runs, it will skip sending the reminder for that loan. [6][7]

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/Loan.java:50-52, src/main/java/org/acme/library/loan/Loan.java:82-84

### reminder-lead

The reminder is sent 2 days before the due date, as specified in the `LibraryProperties` class [3].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/LibraryProperties.java:9-25

### email-retry

Failed emails are retried up to three times with exponential backoff in the `SmtpNotificationGateway` class [6].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/notify/SmtpNotificationGateway.java:12-66

### email-give-up

After the last email delivery attempt fails, the failure is logged and swallowed. The method `SmtpNotificationGateway#send(String, String, String)` catches `MailException` and logs an error message indicating the failure to send an email to the recipient after the maximum number of attempts (3) [4]. The error message includes the recipient's email and the exception message. The method then returns without rethrowing the exception, ensuring that a missed reminder does not fail the batch job that triggered it [2].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/notify/SmtpNotificationGateway.java:32-55, src/main/java/org/acme/library/notify/SmtpNotificationGateway.java:12-66

### email-validation

Email addresses are validated using a regular expression defined in the `EMAIL` pattern in the `MemberService` class [1]. The pattern checks for a valid email format, allowing case-insensitive matching.

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MemberService.java:25-35

### email-unique

No, two members cannot register with the same email in different letter case. The `register` method in `MemberService` normalizes the email to lowercase before checking for uniqueness [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MemberService.java:25-35

### new-member-tier

A newly registered member starts on the STANDARD tier [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/member/MembershipTier.java:3-26

### typo-search

The catalogue search tolerates typos in titles by using a typo-tolerant title search algorithm. This algorithm compares each title word to each query word using the Levenshtein edit distance. A word matches the query term if the Levenshtein distance is at most one edit per four characters [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/search/CatalogSearch.java:11-70

### levenshtein

The Levenshtein edit distance is implemented in the `CatalogSearch` class, specifically in the `levenshtein` method. This method uses a dynamic programming approach with two rolling rows to calculate the edit distance between two strings. [1]

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/search/CatalogSearch.java:50-68

### search-limit

The book search endpoint returns a maximum of 100 results. This is enforced by the `Math.min(limit, 100)` call in the `BookController#search` method [5].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/web/BookController.java:47-51

### checkout-endpoint

The endpoint that checks out a book is `/api/books/checkout` [3].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/web/BookController.java:19-53

### conflict-errors

The `ApiErrorHandler` class maps the following exceptions to HTTP status code 409 Conflict:

- `LoanLimitExceededException`
- `BookUnavailableException`
- `AlreadyBorrowedException`
- `RenewalNotAllowedException`
- `DuplicateEmailException`

These mappings are defined in the `conflict(RuntimeException ex)` method [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/web/ApiErrorHandler.java:30-35

The time zone used for dates is Europe/London, as specified in the `ClockConfig` class [1].

Citations: src/main/java/org/acme/library/config/ClockConfig.java:13-16
